title: Opinion | June 12: We've seen this descent before, report raises many questions and other letters to the editor
subtitle: Hamilton police were shooting at Erixon Kabera and, apparently, each other. This is disturbing, a reader writes
article: Re: SIU clears officers who fatally shot Erixon Kabera eight times in hallway, June 7

The Spectator's story about the SIU report into the police shooting of Erixon Kabera answers some of the questions around the incident. However, the story raises several new and very disturbing questions that go unanswered.
Let's connect the dots from the facts of the report:

Since all of the bullets fired came from police weapons, it means that one Hamilton police officer shot the other police officer in the back of the head. An inch one way or the other and there could have been two dead people in that hallway - Mr. Kabera and a Hamilton police officer.

So the narrative that police were shooting in response to shots from Mr. Kabera is not possible because Mr. Kabera did not have a real gun. In other words, Hamilton police were shooting at Mr. Kabera and, apparently, each other.

This is disturbing. How could it be that one police officer shot the other police officer in the back of the head? How did that happen? How were they positioned in the hallway? How and why did the officers both manage to fall separately? Was that what caused one officer to shoot the other officer? Does all of this highlight some training issues?
If the SIU report was meant to close the book on this incident, I'm afraid it's done the opposite.
